When you sell goods from your Kundarak Vault, the buyer pays you 20 percent more than the standard price; this profit increases to 50 percent when you reach level 13 and 100 percent when you reach level 17.

facility.name: Laboratory
entries: A Laboratory contains storage space for alchemical supplies and workspaces for crafting various concoctions.

entries.name: Craft Options
entries: When you issue the {@book Craft|XDMG|7|Craft} order to this facility, choose one of the following options:

items.name: Craft:
items.entry: Alchemist's Supplies. The facility's hireling crafts anything that can be made with {@item Alchemist's Supplies|XPHB} using the rules in the {@book Player's Handbook|XPHB} and {@book chapter 7|XDMG|6} of this book.

items.name: Craft:
items.entry: Poison. You commission the facility's hireling to craft a vial containing one application of a poison. The poison must be one of the following: {@item Burnt Othur Fumes|XDMG}, {@item Essence of Ether|XDMG}, or {@item Torpor|XDMG}. This work takes 7 days, and you must pay half the poison's cost. See "{@book Poison|XDMG|2|Poison}" in {@book chapter 3|XDMG|2} for descriptions and costs of poisons.

facility.name: Library
entries: This Library contains a collection of books plus one or more desks and reading chairs.

entries.name: Research: Topical Lore
entries: When you issue the {@book Research|XDMG|7|Research} order to this facility, you commission the facility's hireling to research a topic. The topic can be a legend, a known event or location, a person of significance, a type of creature, or a famous object. The work takes 7 days. When the research concludes, the hireling obtains up to three accurate pieces of information about the topic that were previously unknown to you and shares this knowledge with you the next time you speak with them. The DM determines what information you learn.

facility.name: Lighthouse
entries: This tall lighthouse has rotating lenses that make its light visible from a significant distance, even in poor weather. Your hireling operates and maintains the machinery and ignites or douses the light as you direct.

entries.name: Vision Charm
entries: Time in your lighthouse inspires you to pierce the darkness. After spending a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB} in your Lighthouse, you gain the {@reward Charm of Darkvision|XDMG} (see the {@book Dungeon Master's Guide|XDMG}).

entries.name: Harvest: Illuminate Treasure
entries: When you issue the {@book Harvest|XDMG|7|Harvest} order to this facility, you instruct the facility's hireling to watch the surrounding area for lost or discarded valuables. The hireling watches for 7 days. At the end of that time, you can hire salvagers to retrieve treasures your hireling spotted. You must spend 100 GP to hire the salvagers, who return with treasure worth {@dice 1d4 × 100} GP.

facility.name: Lightning Generator
entries: A Lightning Generator can transform atmospheric electricity to serve a variety of useful functions.

entries.name: Charm of Electromancy
entries: After spending a Long Rest in your Lightning Generator, you take {@damage 8d6} Lightning damage and you gain a magical {@reward Charm of Electromancy|RHW|Charm} that lasts for 7 days (see the {@book Dungeon Master's Guide|XDMG} for rules on {@book Charms|XDMG|2|Charms}). The Charm has 3 charges. You can expend 1 charge from the Charm to cast the {@spell Telekinesis|XPHB} spell. Once all its charges are expended, the Charm vanishes from you.

entries.name: Revivification
entries: When you cast the spell {@spell Raise Dead|XPHB} and {@spell Resurrection|XPHB} while in this facility, the cost of that spell's Material components are reduced by 1,000 GP (minimum of 0).

entries.name: Empower: Lightning Life
entries: The facility's hireling channels the Generator's energy to cast {@spell Animate Objects|XPHB}, targeting one Large or Huge object of your choice in the Bastion. The spell's duration is 7 days and doesn't require {@status Concentration|XPHB}.

facility.name: Liminal Space
entries: Your Bastion becomes connected to an unfathomable demiplane filled with vast, empty spaces and strange beings. This special facility doesn't take up space in your Bastion; instead, the entrance to this facility appears in the closets, crawlspaces, and shadows of your Bastion's other basic and special facilities. The hireling in charge of this facility protects the Bastion's inhabitants from stray entities that slip out from the demiplane. This facility always counts as Haunted.

entries.name: Dark Bargains
entries: You can enter this facility and wander within for 7 days, consulting and bargaining with the strange entities there. If you leave the Bastion during this time, you gain no benefit. At the end of the seventh day, you gain a {@filter Dark Gift|feats|category=DG} feat of your choice. You can only have one feat from this benefit at a time; if you use this benefit when you already have a feat from it, the feat you gain at the end of the seven days replaces any feat previously gained from use of this facility.

entries.name: Recruit: Stranger
entries: When you issue the Recruit order to this facility, you instruct the facility's hireling to conduct a ritual and petition an entity from the demiplane for aid. This ritual takes 7 days and costs 1,000 GP. At the ritual's end, roll any die. On an odd number, the summoned entity refuses your request and kills the hireling, and this facility can't be used until your next Bastion turn, at which point the hireling is replaced at no cost to you; on an even number, the summoned entity agrees to your request and takes up residence in your Liminal Space.

While residing in your Liminal Space, an entity counts as a Bastion Defender, and if your Bastion is attacked, each entity in your Liminal Space reduces by 1 the number of dice you roll to determine how many Bastion Defenders are lost in the attack. You can choose not to count the entity as a Bastion Defender, in which case you can't call on it to defend the Bastion; instead, the entity acts according to its nature, using the {@creature Unspeakable Horror|RHW} stat block. You can have up to three entities in your Liminal Space at a time. Deduct any you lose from your Bastion Defenders roster.

facility.name: Lords' Alliance Noble Residence
entries: You maintain a luxurious apartment fit for the ruler of a city such as Neverwinter, Waterdeep, or Baldur's Gate. Your hireling is a butler who tends to the resident's needs.
After spending a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB} in your Noble Residence, you gain {@variantrule Heroic Inspiration|XPHB}.

entries.name: Recruit: Visiting Noble
entries: When you issue the Recruit order to your Lords' Alliance Noble Residence, you forgo sleeping in it for 14 days and instead make it available to a noble from a settlement that is a member of the Lords' Alliance. Roll any die. If the number rolled is odd, no one accepts your invitation and you gain no benefit from having issued the order. If the number rolled is even, a noble from the settlement you chose accepts your invitation, arriving within 7 days and staying for another 7 days.

The visiting noble gossips about events and inhabitants in their home settlement, revealing to you the location of any creature familiar to you if that creature is within 50 miles of the settlement from which the noble has come, if that creature isn't hidden by magic, and if that creature isn't confined to a location that the DM deems beyond the noble's ability to know. If the noble knows the location of the individual, they also tell you where that creature was for the 7 days prior to the noble's departure for your Bastion.
The visiting noble won't defend your Bastion and departs immediately if the Bastion is attacked.

facility.name: Lyrandar Helm
entries: A Lyrandar Helm allows a mobile Bastion built within an elemental airship or an elemental galleon to travel. This facility's hireling is a {@book dragonmarked heir of House Lyrandar|EFA|5|House Lyrandar}. On an elemental airship, the airship's {@book Helm|EFA|7|Helm} crew station is part of this facility (see {@book chapter 7|EFA|7|Crew Members and Stations}).

entries.name: Empower: Travel
entries: When you issue the Empower order to this facility, you instruct its hireling to pilot the Bastion to a destination you specify. The Bastion travels at the vehicle's speed, 8 hours per day, for the duration of the Bastion turn. The Bastion stops early when it reaches the specified destination or if something happens to stop your travel.
When you issue the Empower order to this facility, the DM rolls on the {@book Bastion Events table|XDMG|7|Bastion Events} as if you had issued the Maintain order to your Bastion.

facility.name: Manifest Zone
entries: A Bastion with a Manifest Zone is infused with the planar energy of one of Eberron's planes of existence. Choose the plane when you build this facility.

entries.name: Empower: Manifest Charm
entries: When you issue the Empower order to this facility, the facility's hireling conducts magical rites for the next 7 days. At the end of that period, you gain a special {@filter Charm|rewards|type=charm} (see "{@book Supernatural Gifts|XDMG|2|Supernatural Gifts}" in the {@book Dungeon Master's Guide|XDMG}) called a Manifest Charm, which lasts until you use it. You don't need to be in the Bastion while the rites are performed to gain their benefit. The effects of the Charm depend on the facility's linked plane:

items: {@reward Manifest Charm of Daanvi, the Perfect Order|EFA} ({@book Daanvi, the Perfect Order|ERLW|10|Daanvi, the Perfect Order})
{@reward Manifest Charm of Dolurrh, the Realm of the Dead|EFA} ({@book Dolurrh, the Realm of the Dead|ERLW|10|Dolurrh, the Realm of the Dead})
{@reward Manifest Charm of Fernia, the Sea of Fire|EFA} ({@book Fernia, the Sea of Fire|ERLW|10|Fernia, the Sea of Fire})
{@reward Manifest Charm of Irian, the Eternal Dawn|EFA} ({@book Irian, the Eternal Dawn|ERLW|10|Irian, the Eternal Dawn})
{@reward Manifest Charm of Lamannia, the Twilight Forest|EFA} ({@book Lamannia, the Twilight Forest|ERLW|10|Lamannia, the Twilight Forest})
{@reward Manifest Charm of Mabar, the Endless Night|EFA} ({@book Mabar, the Endless Night|ERLW|10|Mabar, the Endless Night})
{@reward Manifest Charm of Risia, the Plain of Ice|EFA} ({@book Risia, the Plain of Ice|ERLW|10|Risia, the Plain of Ice})
{@reward Manifest Charm of Shavarath, the Battleground|EFA} ({@book Shavarath, the Battleground|ERLW|10|Shavarath, the Battleground})
{@reward Manifest Charm of Syrania, the Azure Sky|EFA} ({@book Syrania, the Azure Sky|ERLW|10|Syrania, the Azure Sky})
{@reward Manifest Charm of Thelanis, the Faerie Court|EFA} ({@book Thelanis, the Faerie Court|ERLW|10|Thelanis, the Faerie Court})
{@reward Manifest Charm of Xoriat, the Realm of Delirium|EFA} ({@book Xoriat, the Realm of Delirium|ERLW|10|Xoriat, the Realm of Madness})

entries: If your Bastion is mobile, its connection to the linked plane of existence is suspended while the Bastion moves, and you can't issue the Empower order to this facility while it is in transit. When the Bastion reaches a destination, you can issue the Empower order to establish a new planar connection, linking the Bastion either to the same plane of existence or to a different one you choose. Establishing the new connection takes 7 days, after which you can issue the Empower order normally.

facility.name: Meditation Chamber
entries: A Meditation Chamber is a relaxing space that helps align one's mind, body, and spirit.

entries.name: Empower: Inner Peace
entries: When you issue the {@book Empower|XDMG|7|Empower} order to this facility, your Bastion's hirelings can use the Meditation Chamber to gain a measure of inner peace. The next time you roll for a Bastion event, you can roll twice and choose either result.

entries.name: Fortify Self
entries: You can meditate in this facility over a period of 7 days. If you leave the Bastion during this time, you gain no benefit. Otherwise, at the end of the seventh day, you gain {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on two kinds of saving throws for the next 7 days, determined randomly by rolling on the table below. Reroll if you get a duplicate result.

facility.name: Menagerie
entries: A Menagerie has enclosures big enough to contain up to four Large creatures. Four Small or Medium creatures can occupy the same space as one Large creature there.

entries.name: Recruit: Creature
entries: When you issue the {@book Recruit|XDMG|7|Recruit} order to this facility, you commission the facility's hirelings to add a creature from the Menagerie Creatures table to your Menagerie. The recruitment takes 7 days and costs you the amount listed in the table. The hirelings look after the creature.

Creatures in your Menagerie count as Bastion Defenders. Deduct any you lose from your Bastion Defenders roster. You can choose not to count one or more of these creatures as Bastion Defenders, in which case they can't be called on to defend the Bastion. Instead, they act in accordance with their nature and use their stat blocks in the {@book Monster Manual|XMM}.

With the DM's consent, you can add different creatures than those shown in the Menagerie Creatures table to your Menagerie. The cost of a creature depends on its {@variantrule Challenge Rating|XPHB}, as shown on the Creature Costs by Challenge Rating table. Typically only Beasts and some Monstrosities can be kept in a Menagerie, though the DM might allow other creatures.

facility.name: Morgue
entries: A morgue is a location where corpses are stored and studied. You can store up to four Small or Medium corpses in the Morgue.

entries.name: Corpse Storage
entries: As long as this facility's hireling is present, each corpse stored in the Morgue is affected by the {@spell Gentle Repose|XPHB} spell. If the facility lacks a hireling or a corpse is removed, the facility's corpses or the removed corpse loses this protection until returned to a Morgue with a hireling.

entries.name: Research: Cadaver Insights
entries: When you issue the {@book Research|XDMG|7|Research} order to this facility, you instruct the facility's hireling to carefully inspect the corpses. This work takes 7 days. The next time you speak with the hireling, the hireling can share the cause of death of each corpse present and answer one question you have for each corpse as though the hireling had cast the {@spell Speak with Dead|XPHB} spell on it.

entries.name: Enlarging the Facility
entries: You can enlarge your Morgue to a Roomy facility by spending 2,000 GP. If you do so, the Morgue can store up to twelve Small or Medium corpses and up to one Large corpse.

facility.name: Museum
entries: A Museum contains relics and treasures brought back from expeditions you participated in or sponsored, carefully cataloged and displayed.

entries.name: Research: Specialized Lore
entries: When you issue the Research order to this facility, you commission the hireling to study particular treasures in the museum. The work takes 7 days. The hireling gains knowledge regarding some question of ancient history as if they had cast the {@spell Legend Lore|XPHB} spell, then shares this knowledge with you the next time you speak with them.

entries.name: Secrets of the Past
entries: Your Museum contains one treasure that gives you a magical {@filter Charm|rewards|type=charm} (see "{@book Supernatural Gifts|XDMG|2|Supernatural Gifts}" in the {@book Dungeon Master's Guide|XDMG}) when you spend 7 days studying it and then finish a Long Rest in your Bastion. The Charm lasts for 7 days or until you use it. You can't gain another Charm from this facility while you still have one. The effect of the Charm depends on the origin of the treasure in your Museum. You can choose one of the following options (your DM might make more options available or limit the existing options based on your past expeditions):

items: {@reward Charm of Argonnessen|EFA}
{@reward Charm of Ashtakala|EFA}
{@reward Charm of Dhakaan|EFA}
{@reward Charm of Khyber|EFA}
{@reward Charm of Xen'drik|EFA}

entries.name: Enlarging the Facility
entries: You can enlarge your Museum to a Vast facility by spending 2,000 GP. If you do so, the Museum can have two treasures with different origins. A Vast Museum gains two additional hirelings, for a total of three. Assign names and personalities to them as you see fit.

facility.name: Navigator's Helm
entries: A Navigator's Helm allows a mobile Bastion built within a mundane waterborne vehicle to travel.

entries.name: Empower: Travel
entries: When you issue the Empower order to this facility, you instruct its hireling to pilot the Bastion to a destination you specify. The Bastion sails at the vehicle's speed, 8 hours per day, for the duration of the Bastion turn. The Bastion stops early when it reaches the specified destination or if something happens to stop your travel.
When you issue the Empower order to this facility, the DM rolls on the {@book Bastion Events table|XDMG|7|Bastion Events} as if you had issued the Maintain order to your Bastion.

facility.name: Observatory
entries: Situated atop your Bastion, your Observatory contains a telescope aimed at the night sky.

entries.name: Observatory Charm
entries: You can use your Observatory to peer into the far corners of {@book Wildspace|XDMG|5|Wildspace} and the {@book Astral Plane|XDMG|5|Astral Plane}. After spending a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB} in your Observatory, you gain a magical {@reward Observatory Charm|XDMG|Charm} (see "{@book Supernatural Gifts|XDMG|2|Supernatural Gifts}" in {@book chapter 3|XDMG|2}) that lasts for 7 days or until you use it. The Charm allows you to cast {@spell Contact Other Plane|XPHB} without expending a spell slot. You can't gain this Charm again while you still have it.

entries.name: Empower: Eldritch Discovery
entries: When you issue the {@book Empower|XDMG|7|Empower} order to this facility, you enable yourself or the facility's hireling to explore the eldritch mysteries of the stars for 7 consecutive nights. At the end of that time, roll a die. If the number rolled is even, nothing is gained. If the number rolled is odd, an unknown power bestows one of the following Charms on you or another creature of your choice that is on the same plane of existence as you: {@reward Charm of Darkvision|XDMG}, {@reward Charm of Heroism|XDMG}, or {@reward Charm of Vitality|XDMG} (all described in {@book chapter 3|XDMG|2}).

facility.name: Order of the Gauntlet Tournament Field
entries: The Order of the Gauntlet Tournament Field is a marked-off area for combat between two armed individuals. It includes room for spectators.

Your hireling is a {@creature Knight|XMM} whose alignment matches your own. If your Bastion lacks facilities to house this knight, the knight secures accommodations in the inn or settlement closest to the Bastion. This knight isn't a Bastion Defender, but if your Bastion is attacked, the knight reduces by 1 the number of dice you roll to determine how many Bastion Defenders are lost in the attack.

entries.name: Empower: Hold Tournament
entries: When you issue the {@book Empower|XDMG|7|Empower} order to this facility, you host a tournament at your Bastion. It takes 7 days for word of the tournament to spread to nearby settlements, and another 7 days for contestants to travel to your Bastion and participate in the tournament. You must spend 2,000 GP for prizes. At the conclusion of the tournament, your Renown Score with the Order of the Gauntlet increases by 1.

facility.name: Orien Helm
entries: An Orien Helm allows a mobile Bastion built within a Lightning Rail cart to travel. This facility's hireling is a {@book dragonmarked heir of House Orien|EFA|5|House Orien}.

entries.name: Empower: Travel
entries: When you issue the Empower order to this facility, you instruct its hireling to pilot the Bastion to a destination you specify. The Bastion travels at a rate of 30 miles per hour, 8 hours per day, along an existing route of conductor stones for the duration of the Bastion turn. The Bastion stops early when it reaches the specified destination or if something happens to stop your travel.
When you issue the Empower order to this facility, the DM rolls on the {@book Bastion Events table|XDMG|7|Bastion Events} as if you had issued the Maintain order to your Bastion.

facility.name: Parlor
entries: A basic facility comes with nonmagical furnishings and decor appropriate for that facility.

facility.name: Planar Gateway
entries: The focus of this chamber is an inscribed stone archway filled with mist and strange lights. This archway can connect to other planes of existence.

entries.name: Empower: Open Gate
entries: When you issue the {@book Empower|XDMG|7|Empower} order to this facility, you instruct the facility's hireling to tune the archway to a place on another plane of existence. Tuning the archway takes 7 days, at the end of which time the gateway opens. If you provide a diamond worth 5,000+ GP as part of the tuning, the gate connects to a place you specify on another plane, as with the {@spell Gate|XPHB} spell (for transport only, not to draw a specific creature through) and destroys the diamond. If you don't provide a diamond or if a deity or another planar ruler blocks the intended gate from opening, determine the gate's destination randomly on the Random Planar Destination table. In either case, the gateway remains open for 1 minute.

entries.caption: Random Planar Destination
rows: {@book Elemental Plane of Air|XDMG|5|Elemental Plane of Air}
{@book Elemental Plane of Earth|XDMG|5|Elemental Plane of Earth}
{@book Elemental Plane of Fire|XDMG|5|Elemental Plane of Fire}
{@book Elemental Plane of Water|XDMG|5|Elemental Plane of Water}

facility.name: Pub
entries: Folks come here to consume tasty beverages and socialize. Your Pub might be a bar, coffee shop, or tea room, and it might have a colorful name, such as the Rusty Flagon or the Dragon's Loft. The facility's hireling, who serves as the bartender, maintains a network of spies scattered throughout nearby communities. These spies are useful sources of information and frequent the Pub, often incognito.

entries.name: Research: Information Gathering
entries: When you issue the {@book Research|XDMG|7|Research} order to this facility, you commission the Pub's bartender to gather information from spies who are aware of all important events happening within 10 miles of your Bastion over the next 7 days. During that time, these spies can divulge the location of any creature that is familiar to you, provided the creature is within 50 miles of your Bastion and not hidden by magic or confined to a location that the DM deems is beyond the spy network's ability to locate. If the spies learn the target's location, they also learn where that creature has been for the previous 7 days.

entries.name: Pub Special
entries: The Pub has one magical beverage on tap, chosen from the options below:

items.name: Bigby's Burden
items.entry: Drinking a pint of this beverage grants you the "enlarge" effect of an {@spell Enlarge/Reduce|XPHB} spell that has a duration of 24 hours (no saving throw allowed).

items.name: Kiss of the Spider Queen
items.entry: Drinking a pint of this beverage grants you the effect of a {@spell Spider Climb|XPHB} spell that has a duration of 24 hours.

items.name: Moonlight Serenade
items.entry: Drinking a pint of this beverage gives you {@sense Darkvision|XPHB} out to 60 feet for 24 hours. If you already have {@sense Darkvision|XPHB}, its range is extended by 60 feet for the same duration.

items.name: Positive Reinforcement
items.entry: Drinking a pint of this beverage gives you {@variantrule Resistance|XPHB} to Necrotic damage for 24 hours.

items.name: Sterner Stuff
items.entry: For 24 hours after drinking a pint of this beverage, you automatically succeed on saving throws to avoid or end the {@condition Frightened|XPHB} condition.

entries: At the start of a Bastion turn, you can switch to one of the other options. Your DM may create new options. A pint of this magical beverage loses its magic 24 hours after it's poured.

entries.name: Enlarging the Facility
entries: You can enlarge your Pub to a Vast facility by spending 2,000 GP. If you do so, the Pub can have two magical beverages from the Pub Special list on tap at a time. A Vast Pub gains three additional hirelings, for a total of four. These new hirelings are servers. Assign names and personalities to them as you see fit.

facility.name: Red Wizard Necropolis
entries: Red Wizards defend their strongholds with Undead minions. A Red Wizard Necropolis can accommodate up to eight Bastion Defenders.

entries.name: Recruit: Undead Defenders
entries: Each time you issue the Recruit action to this facility, up to four Undead Bastion Defenders are created and take shelter in the crypts and burial chambers of your Red Wizard Necropolis. You can't issue the Recruit order to this facility if it's fully occupied.

Keep track of Undead Bastion Defenders you lose and deduct them from your Bastion Defenders roster. An Undead Bastion Defender returns to your Red Wizard Necropolis 14 days after being destroyed. Undead Bastion Defenders can't return from being killed if the facility is shut down or fully occupied.

facility.name: Reliquary
entries: This vault holds sacred objects.

entries.name: Reliquary Charm
entries: After spending a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB} in your Bastion, you gain a magical {@reward Reliquary Charm|XDMG|Charm} (see "{@book Supernatural Gifts|XDMG|2|Supernatural Gifts}" in {@book chapter 3|XDMG|2}) that lasts for 7 days or until you use it. The Charm allows you to cast {@spell Greater Restoration|XPHB} once without expending a spell slot or using Material components. You can't gain this Charm again while you still have it.

entries.name: Harvest: Talisman
entries: When you issue the {@book Harvest|XDMG|7|Harvest} order to this facility, you commission its hireling to produce a specially prepared talisman for your use. The talisman usually takes the form of an amulet, a rune-carved box, or a statuette, but it can be any Tiny, nonmagical object that has religious significance. The work takes 7 days and costs no money. You can use this talisman in place of one spell's Material components, provided the components have a cost of 1,000 GP or less. If the spell normally consumes its components, the talisman isn't consumed. After the talisman has been used in this way, it can't be used again until you return it to your Reliquary and use another Harvest order to prepare it.

facility.name: Rookery
entries: A number of ravens equal to your character level roost in a Rookery. Whenever a creature enters the facility, the birds uncannily track its movement, an unfathomable intelligence behind their beady eyes.

entries.name: Craft: Mist Talisman
entries: When you issue the Craft order to this facility, you can commission the hireling to send ravens to various contacts in a Domain of Dread you have either visited previously or heard about from a creature that has been within said domain. This work takes 21 days, during which time no other activity can occur within this facility.
At the end of this period, the hireling produces a {@book Mist talisman|RHW|0|Mist Talismans} linked to the chosen Domain of Dread.

entries.name: Messenger Ravens
entries: Whenever you finish a Long Rest in your Bastion, you can send one raven bearing a written message of 25 words or fewer to a creature you have met or a creature described to you by someone who has met it. After receiving this message, the recipient can reply in a like manner, attaching their response to the raven. Regardless of whether or not the recipient responds, the raven returns to the rookery after 7 days have passed.

You can send a message via raven in this way across any distance, though the message recipient must be on the same plane of existence as your Bastion or in a demiplane linked to yours by the Mists of Ravenloft. A messenger raven delivers the message regardless of any magical wards or other interposing forces, including the Mists and closed borders of a Domain of Dread. If the raven is unable to deliver your message, it returns to your rookery after 7 days with your original message still attached.

facility.name: Sacristy
entries: A Sacristy serves as a preparation and storage room for the sacred items and religious vestments.

entries.name: Craft Options
entries: When you issue the {@book Craft|XDMG|7|Craft} order to this facility, choose one of the following options:

items.name: Craft:
items.entry: Holy Water. You commission the facility's hireling to craft a flask of {@item Holy Water|XPHB}. The work takes 7 days and costs no money. You can spend GP during the creation process to increase the potency of the Holy Water. For every 100 GP you spend, up to a maximum of 500 GP, the damage dealt by the Holy Water increases by {@damage 1d8}.

items.name: Craft:
items.entry: Magic Item (Relic). You commission the facility's hireling to craft a Common or an Uncommon magic item chosen by you from the {@book Relics|XDMG|6|Relics Tables} tables in {@book chapter 7|XDMG|6}. The facility has the tool required to craft the item, and the hireling has proficiency with that tool as well as proficiency in the {@skill Arcana|XPHB} skill. See the "{@book Crafting Magic Items|XDMG|6|Crafting Magic Items}" section in {@book chapter 7|XDMG|6} for the time and money that must be spent to craft the item. If the item allows its user to cast any spells from it, you must craft the item yourself (the facility's hireling can assist), and you must have all those spells prepared every day you spend crafting the item.

entries.name: Spell Refreshment
entries: Having a Sacristy allows you to regain one expended spell slot of level 5 or lower after spending an entire {@variantrule Short Rest|XPHB} in your Bastion. You can't gain this benefit again until you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

facility.name: Sanctuary
entries: Icons of your religion are displayed in this facility, which includes a quiet place for worship.

entries.name: Sanctuary Charm
entries: After spending a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB} in your Bastion, you gain a magical {@reward Sanctuary Charm|XDMG|Charm} (see "{@book Supernatural Gifts|XDMG|2|Supernatural Gifts}" in {@book chapter 3|XDMG|2}) that lasts for 7 days or until you use it. The Charm allows you to cast {@spell Healing Word|XPHB} once without expending a spell slot. You can't gain this Charm again while you still have it.

entries.name: Craft: Sacred Focus
entries: When you issue the {@book Craft|XDMG|7|Craft} order to this facility, you commission the facility's hireling to craft a {@item Druidic Focus|XPHB} ({@item wooden staff|XPHB}) or a {@item Holy Symbol|XPHB}. The work takes 7 days and costs no money. The item remains in your Bastion until you claim it.

facility.name: Sanctum
entries: A Sanctum is a place of solace and healing.

entries.name: Sanctum Charm
entries: After spending a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB} in your Bastion, you gain a magical {@reward Sanctum Charm|XDMG|Charm} (see "{@book Supernatural Gifts|XDMG|2|Supernatural Gifts}" in {@book chapter 3|XDMG|2}) that lasts for 7 days or until you use it. The Charm allows you to cast {@spell Heal|XPHB} once without expending a spell slot. You can't gain this Charm again while you still have it.

entries.name: Empower: Fortifying Rites
entries: When you issue the {@book Empower|XDMG|7|Empower} order to this facility, you inspire its hirelings to perform daily rites that benefit you or another character you name. The beneficiary doesn't need to be in the Bastion when the rites are performed to gain their benefit. Each time the beneficiary finishes a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}, they gain {@variantrule Temporary Hit Points|XPHB} equal to your level. This effect lasts for 7 days.

entries.name: Sanctum Recall
entries: While the Sanctum exists, you always have the {@spell Word of Recall|XPHB} spell prepared. When you cast {@spell Word of Recall|XPHB}, you can make your Sanctum the destination of the spell instead of another place you have previously designated. In addition, one creature of your choice that arrives in the Sanctum via this spell gains the benefit of a {@spell Heal|XPHB} spell.

facility.name: Scriptorium
entries: A Scriptorium contains desks and writing supplies.

entries.name: Craft Options
entries: When you issue the {@book Craft|XDMG|7|Craft} order to this facility, choose one of the following options:

items.name: Craft:
items.entry: Book Replica. You commission the facility's hireling to make a copy of a nonmagical Book. Doing so requires a blank book. The work takes 7 days.

items.name: Craft:
items.entry: Spell Scroll. You commission the facility's hireling to scribe a {@item Spell Scroll|XDMG} containing one Cleric or Wizard spell of level 3 or lower. The facility has the necessary {@item Calligrapher's Supplies|XPHB}, and the hireling meets all the prerequisites needed to scribe the scroll. The "{@book Crafting Equipment|XPHB|6|Crafting Equipment}" section in the {@book Player's Handbook|XPHB} specifies the time needed to scribe the scroll and the cost of the scroll, which you must pay.

items.name: Craft:
items.entry: Paperwork. You commission the facility's hireling to create up to fifty copies of a broadsheet, a pamphlet, or another loose-leaf paper product. The work takes 7 days and costs you 1 GP per copy. At no additional cost in time or money, the facility's hireling can distribute the paperwork to one or more locations within 50 miles of your Bastion.

facility.name: Smithy
entries: This Smithy contains a forge, an anvil, and other tools needed to craft weapons, armor, and other equipment.

entries.name: Craft Options
entries: When you issue the {@book Craft|XDMG|7|Craft} order to this facility, choose one of the following options:

items.name: Craft:
items.entry: Smith's Tools. The facility's hirelings craft anything that can be made with {@item Smith's Tools|XPHB}, using the rules in the {@book Player's Handbook|XPHB}.

items.name: Craft:
items.entry: Magic Item (Armament). If you are level 9+, you can commission the facility's hirelings to craft a Common or an Uncommon magic item chosen by you from the {@book Armaments|XDMG|6|Armaments Tables} tables in {@book chapter 7|XDMG|6}. The facility has the tool required to craft the item, and the hirelings have proficiency with that tool as well as proficiency in the {@skill Arcana|XPHB} skill. See the "{@book Crafting Magic Items|XDMG|6|Crafting Magic Items}" section in {@book chapter 7|XDMG|6} for the time and money that must be spent to craft the item. If the item allows its user to cast any spells from it, you must craft the item yourself (the facility's hirelings can assist), and you must have all those spells prepared every day you spend crafting the item.

facility.name: Soup Kitchen
entries: This kitchen prepares large quantities of food and serves it to hungry people.

entries.name: Recruit: Kitchen Operation
entries: When you issue the {@book Recruit|XDMG|7|Recruit} order to this facility, you instruct your hireling to operate the soup kitchen for 7 days. Ingredients cost you 50 GP. If you would lose a Bastion Defender or a hireling on the next roll on the {@book Bastion Events|XDMG|7|Bastion Events} table, someone who believes in your work steps into their place and takes over immediately. You don't count as losing that Bastion Defender or hireling.

entries.name: Traveling Snacks
entries: After spending a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB} in your Bastion, you gain a magical {@reward Traveling Snacks|AU|Charm} that lasts for 7 days or until you use it. The Charm allows you to cast {@spell Goodberry|XPHB} once without expending a spell slot.

facility.name: Spirit Vault
entries: A Spirit Vault is magically warded to imprison and exorcise malevolent spirits and other supernatural forces. Haunted portraits, cursed relics, and other eerie curios line the shelves of this dark vault. This facility always counts as Haunted.

entries.name: Esoteric Knowledge
entries: After spending a Long Rest in your Spirit Vault, you gain one of the following magical Charms:

items: {@reward Charm of Exorcism|RHW}
{@reward Charm of Malediction|RHW}

entries: The Charm lasts for 7 days or until you use it. Intelligence, Wisdom, or Charisma is your spellcasting ability for the Charm's spells (choose each time you gain this Charm).

entries.name: Research: Ask the Occult
entries: When you issue the Research order to this facility, you or its hireling study the various relics and question the imprisoned entities within your Spirit Vault. This work takes 7 days. At the end of this time, roll {@dice 1d6}. On a 1, the work is psychically taxing; if you did the research, you take {@damage 6d6} Psychic damage, and if the hireling did the research, they immediately die, and this facility can't be used again until your next Bastion turn. Otherwise, you or the hireling gain information as if you had successfully cast the {@spell Contact Other Plane|XPHB} spell. The hireling shares any information they learned with you the next time you speak.

facility.name: Stable
entries: A Bastion can have more than one Stable. Each Stable you add to your Bastion comes with one {@creature Riding Horse|XMM} or {@creature Camel|XMM} and two {@creature Pony|XMM|Ponies} or {@creature Mule|XMM|Mules}; see the {@book Player's Handbook|XPHB} or the {@book Monster Manual|XMM} for these creatures' stat blocks. The facility is big enough to house three Large animals. Two Medium creatures occupy the same amount of space as one Large creature there. The facility's hireling looks after these creatures.
After a Beast that can serve as a mount spends at least 14 days in this facility, all Wisdom ({@skill Animal Handling|XPHB}) checks made with respect to it have {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB}.

entries.name: Trade: Animals
entries: When you issue the {@book Trade|XDMG|7|Trade} order to this facility, you commission the facility's hireling to buy or sell one or more mounts at normal cost, keeping the ones you buy in your Stable. The work takes 7 days, and the DM decides what types of animals are available for purchase—horses, ponies, and mules being the most common. The {@table Mounts and Vehicles; Mounts and Other Animals|XPHB|Mounts and Other Animals} table in the {@book Player's Handbook|XPHB} gives standard prices for various mounts. You bear the total cost of any purchases.

When you sell a mount from your Stable, the buyer pays you 20 percent more than the standard price; this profit increases to 50 percent when you reach level 13 and 100 percent when you reach level 17.

entries.name: Enlarging the Facility
entries: You can enlarge your Stable to a Vast facility by spending 2,000 GP. If you do so, the Stable is large enough to house six Large animals.

facility.name: Storage
entries: A basic facility comes with nonmagical furnishings and decor appropriate for that facility.

facility.name: Storehouse
entries: A Storehouse is a cool, dark space meant to contain trade goods objects from the {@book Trade Goods|XDMG|6|Trade Goods} table in {@book chapter 7|XDMG|6} and from {@book chapter 6|XDMG|5} of the {@book Player's Handbook|XPHB}.

entries.name: Trade: Goods
entries: When you issue the {@book Trade|XDMG|7|Trade} order to this facility, its hireling spends the next 7 days procuring nonmagical items that have a total value of 500 GP or less and stores them in the Storehouse, or the hireling uses those 7 days to sell goods in the Storehouse. You bear the total cost of any purchases, and the maximum value of the items purchased increases to 2,000 GP when you reach level 9 and 5,000 GP when you reach level 13.

When you sell goods from your Storehouse, the buyer pays you 10 percent more than the standard price; this profit increases to 20 percent when you reach level 9, 50 percent when you reach level 13, and 100 percent when you reach level 17.

facility.name: Séance Parlor
entries: The veil between the world of the living and the dead grows thin in a Séance Parlor.

entries.name: Research: Fortune Telling
entries: When you issue the Research order to this facility, you commission its hireling to read your fortune by casting bones, interpreting tea leaves, performing a tarokka reading, or using some other means. After your fortune is read, you gain {@variantrule Heroic Inspiration|XPHB}. You can't gain this benefit again until you finish a Long Rest.

entries.name: Speak with Dead
entries: After spending a Long Rest in your Séance Parlor, you can cast {@spell Speak with Dead|XPHB} immediately without expending a spell slot or needing Material components. When you cast it in this way, you can target any deceased creature whose name you know, as long as you have a piece of its remains (such as ashes or a bone) or an object that was important to the creature in life (such as a brooch or signature weapon). The target speaks through an implement in the Séance Room such as a crystal ball or spirit board.

facility.name: Teleportation Circle
entries: Inscribed on the floor of this room is a permanent teleportation circle created by the {@spell Teleportation Circle|XPHB} spell.

entries.name: Recruit: Spellcaster
entries: Each time you issue the {@book Recruit|XDMG|7|Recruit} order to this facility, its hireling extends an invitation to a {@variantrule Friendly [Attitude]|XPHB|Friendly} NPC spellcaster. Roll any die. If the number rolled is odd, the invitee declines the invitation, and you gain no benefit from having issued the order. If the number rolled is even, the invitee accepts the invitation and arrives in your Bastion via your Teleportation Circle.

While you are in your Bastion, you can ask the spellcaster to cast one Wizard spell of level 4 or lower; if you are level 17+, the spell's maximum level increases to 8. The spellcaster is assumed to have the spell prepared. If the spell has one or more Material components that cost money, you must pay for them before the spell can be cast.

The spellcaster stays for 14 days or until they cast a spell for you. The spellcaster won't defend your Bastion and departs immediately if the Bastion is attacked (see "{@book Bastion Events|XDMG|7|Bastion Events}" at the end of the chapter).

facility.name: Theater
entries: The Theater contains a stage, a backstage area where props and sets are kept, and a seating area for a small audience.

entries.name: Empower: Theatrical Event
entries: When you issue the {@book Empower|XDMG|7|Empower} order to this facility, its hirelings begin work on a theatrical production or concert. Rehearsals and other preparations take 14 days, followed by at least 7 days of performances. The performances can continue indefinitely until a new production gets underway.
You or another character can contribute to a production in the following ways:

items.name: Composer/Writer
items.entry: A character can compose music or write a script for a concert or production that hasn't started rehearsals yet. This effort takes 14 days.

items.name: Conductor/Director
items.entry: A character who remains in the Bastion for the entirety of the production can serve as the concert's conductor or the production's director.

items.name: Performer
items.entry: A character who remains in the Bastion for the entirety of the rehearsal period can be a star performer in one or more of the performances; one of the Theater's hirelings can serve as an understudy for additional performances.

entries: At the end of a rehearsal period, each character who contributed to the concert or production can make a {@dc 15} Charisma ({@skill Performance|XPHB}) check. If more of these checks succeed than fail, you and any other character who contributed to the concert or production each gain a Theater die, a {@dice d6}. This die changes to a {@dice d8} when you reach level 13 and a {@dice d10} when you reach level 17. At any point after the rehearsals end, a character can expend their Theater die to roll it and add the number rolled to one {@variantrule D20 Test|XPHB} they make, immediately after rolling the {@dice d20}. If a character hasn't expended their Theater die before gaining another, their first die is lost.

facility.name: Training Area
entries: A Bastion can have more than one Training Area. A Training Area might be an open courtyard, a gymnasium, a music or dance hall, or a cleverly built gauntlet of traps and hazards. It might contain inanimate targets (for weapon practice), padded mats, and other equipment. One of the facility's hirelings is an expert trainer; the others serve as training partners.
When a Training Area becomes part of your Bastion, choose one trainer from the Expert Trainers table. On each Bastion turn, you can replace that trainer with another one from the table.

entries.caption: Expert Trainers
rows: When you take damage from an attack made with an {@variantrule Unarmed Strike|XPHB} or a weapon, you can take a {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB} to reduce this damage by {@dice 1d4}.

You gain proficiency in one of the following skills of your choice: {@skill Acrobatics|XPHB}, {@skill Athletics|XPHB}, {@skill Performance|XPHB}, {@skill Sleight of Hand|XPHB}, or {@skill Stealth|XPHB}.
You gain proficiency with one tool of your choice.
When you hit with your {@variantrule Unarmed Strike|XPHB} and deal damage, the attack deals an extra {@damage 1d4} Bludgeoning damage.

Choose a kind of Simple or Martial weapon, such as {@item Spear|XPHB} or {@item Longbow|XPHB}. If you aren't proficient with the weapon, you gain proficiency with it. If you already have proficiency with the weapon, you can use its mastery property.

entries.name: Empower: Training
entries: When you issue the {@book Empower|XDMG|7|Empower} order to this facility, the facility's hirelings conduct training exercises for the next 7 days. Any character who trains here for at least 8 hours on each of those days gains a benefit at the end of the training period. The benefit depends on which trainer is present in the facility, as noted in the Expert Trainers table. The benefit lasts for 7 days.

facility.name: Transmutation Vat
entries: This laboratory features a vat or cauldron simmering with transformation potential.

entries.name: Harvest: Fluid Transmutation
entries: When you issue the {@book Harvest|XDMG|7|Harvest} order to this facility, you instruct your hireling to pour a substance into the vat and transform it into something else. You must expend a Common or Uncommon potion, which is destroyed in the vat. At the end of 7 days, the hireling produces your choice of a flask of {@item Alchemist's Fire|XPHB}, a vial of {@item Antitoxin|XPHB}, a vial of {@item Basic Poison|XPHB}, or a Common or Uncommon potion of your choice.

entries.name: Enlarging the Facility
entries: You can enlarge your Transmutation Vat into a Roomy facility by spending 2,000 GP. When you issue the {@book Harvest|XDMG|7|Harvest} order to a Roomy Transmutation Vat, you can expend two Common or Uncommon potions. If you do, your hireling produces two substances of your choice instead of one; the options can be different.

facility.name: Trophy Room
entries: This room houses a collection of mementos, such as weapons from old battles, the mounted heads of slain creatures, trinkets plucked from dungeons and ruins, and trophies passed down from ancestors.

entries.name: Research Options
entries: When you issue the {@book Research|XDMG|7|Research} order to this facility, choose one of the following options:

items.name: Research:
items.entry: Lore. You commission the facility's hireling to research a topic of your choice. The topic can be a legend, any kind of creature, or a famous object. The topic need not be directly related to items on display in the room, as the trophies provide clues to research a wide variety of other subjects. The work takes 7 days. When the research concludes, the hireling obtains up to three accurate pieces of information about the topic that were previously unknown to you and shares this knowledge with you the next time you speak with them. The DM determines what information is learned.

items.name: Research:
items.entry: Trinket Trophy. You commission the facility's hireling to search for a trinket that might be of use to you. The work takes 7 days. When the research concludes, roll any die. If the number rolled is odd, the hireling finds nothing useful. If the number rolled is even, the hireling finds a magic item. Roll on the {@book Implements - Common|XDMG|6|Implements - Common} table in {@book chapter 7|XDMG|6} to determine what it is.

facility.name: War Room

otherSummary.entry: Fighting Style feature or Unarmored Defense feature

entries: The War Room is where you plan military actions in consultation with an inner circle of loyal lieutenants, each one a battle-hardened {@b Veteran Warrior} (see the {@book Monster Manual|XMM}) whose alignment matches yours. You start with two lieutenants but can add more, as described below. If your Bastion lacks facilities to house your lieutenants, they secure accommodations in the inn or settlement closest to your Bastion. Lieutenants are hirelings, not Bastion Defenders; however, if your Bastion is attacked (see "{@book Bastion Events|XDMG|7|Attack}" at the end of this chapter), each lieutenant housed in your Bastion reduces by 1 the number of dice you roll to determine how many Bastion Defenders are lost in the attack.
The War Room contains war memorabilia plus a large table surrounded by enough chairs for you and your lieutenants.

entries.name: Recruit Options
entries: When you issue the {@book Recruit|XDMG|7|Recruit} order to this facility, choose one of the following options:

items.name: Recruit:
items.entry: Lieutenant. You gain one new lieutenant. You can have up to ten lieutenants at any time. Assign names and personalities to them as you see fit.

items.name: Recruit:
items.entry: Soldiers. You commission one or more of your lieutenants to assemble a small army. Each lieutenant can muster one hundred {@creature Guard|XMM|Guards} (see the {@book Monster Manual|XMM}) in 7 days to fight for your cause. Reduce that number to twenty if you want them to be mounted on {@creature Riding Horse|XMM|Riding Horses} (see the {@book Monster Manual|XMM}). It costs you 1 GP per day to feed each guard and each horse in your army. Wherever the army goes, it must be led by you or at least one of your lieutenants, or else it disbands immediately. The army also disbands if it goes 1 day without being fed. Otherwise, the army remains until it is destroyed or you command it to disband. You can't issue this Recruit order again until your current army disbands or is destroyed.

facility.name: Workshop
entries: This Workshop is a creative space where useful items can be crafted.

entries.name: Artisan's Tools
entries: The Workshop comes equipped with six different kinds of {@item Artisan's Tools|XPHB}, chosen from the following list:

items: {@item Carpenter's Tools|XPHB}
{@item Cobbler's Tools|XPHB}
{@item Glassblower's Tools|XPHB}
{@item Jeweler's Tools|XPHB}
{@item Leatherworker's Tools|XPHB}
{@item Mason's Tools|XPHB}
{@item Painter's Supplies|XPHB|Painter's Tools}
{@item Potter's Tools|XPHB}
{@item Tinker's Tools|XPHB}
{@item Weaver's Tools|XPHB}
{@item Woodcarver's Tools|XPHB}

entries.name: Craft Options
entries: When you issue the {@book Craft|XDMG|7|Craft} order to this facility, choose one of the following options:

items.name: Craft:
items.entry: Adventuring Gear. The facility's hirelings craft anything that can be made with the tools you chose when you added the Workshop to your Bastion (see above), using the rules in the {@book Player's Handbook|XPHB}.

items.name: Craft:
items.entry: Magic Item (Implement). If you are level 9+, you can commission the facility's hirelings to craft a Common or an Uncommon magic item chosen by you from the {@book Implements|XDMG|6|Implements Tables} tables in {@book chapter 7|XDMG|6}. The facility has the tool required to craft the item, and the hirelings have proficiency with that tool as well as proficiency in the {@skill Arcana|XPHB} skill. See the "{@book Crafting Magic Items|XDMG|6|Crafting Magic Items}" section in {@book chapter 7|XDMG|6} for the time and money that must be spent to craft the item. If the item allows its user to cast any spells from it, you must craft the item yourself (the facility's hirelings can assist), and you must have all those spells prepared every day you spend crafting the item.

entries.name: Source of Inspiration
entries: After spending an entire {@variantrule Short Rest|XPHB} in your Workshop, you gain {@variantrule Heroic Inspiration|XPHB}. You can't gain this benefit again until you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

entries.name: Enlarging the Facility
entries: You can enlarge your Workshop to a Vast facility by spending 2,000 GP. If you do so, the Workshop gains two additional hirelings and three additional {@item Artisan's Tools|XPHB} (chosen from the list above).

facility.name: Zhentarim Travel Station
entries: The Zhentarim maintain stations to facilitate safe and swift long-distance travel on journeys (see {@book chapter 2|XDMG|1|Travel} of the {@book Dungeon Master's Guide|XDMG}). Your travel station includes temporary stabling facilities for four Large creatures; two Medium creatures occupy the same space as one Large creature there. The facility's hirelings look after these creatures.

entries.name: Long-Distance Travel Speed
entries: Finishing a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB} in your Bastion better prepares you for travel; your group's maximum travel pace increases by one step (from Slow to Normal or from Normal to Fast).

entries.name: Research: Reconnaissance
entries: When you issue the Research order to this facility, you commission the Zhentarim Travel Station's hirelings to gather information that facilitates an upcoming journey. This work takes 7 days. For the duration of the journey, you have {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on Wisdom ({@skill Survival|XPHB}) checks to forage or navigate.

charoption.name: Alagondar Scion

prerequisite.note: If you don't meet this prerequisite, draw a different card.

entries: I'm a scion of the Alagondar bloodline and the only known heir to the crown of Neverwinter. If Dagult Neverember, the city's lord-regent, learns that I'm alive, he'll send assassins to kill me.

charoption.name: Anvilwrought
entries: You were forged in the fires of Purphoros's forge. Your appearance bears a metallic sheen and visible joints. The Anvilwrought Characteristics table suggests details of your life or origins. Additionally, you gain the following traits.

entries.name: Constructed Resilience
entries: You were created to have remarkable fortitude, represented by the following benefits:

items: You have advantage on saving throws against being {@condition poisoned}, and you have resistance to poison damage.
You don't need to eat, drink, or breathe.
You are immune to disease.
You don't need to sleep, and magic can't put you to sleep.

entries.name: Sentry's Rest
entries: When you take a long rest, you must spend at least six hours in an inactive, motionless state, rather than sleeping. In this state, you appear inert, but it doesn't render you {@condition unconscious}, and you can see and hear as normal.

entries.caption: Anvilwrought Characteristics
rows: An oread who works in Purphoros's forge is the closest thing I have to a parent.
Purphoros made me to serve him.
I was created decades ago and, fearing that I'm growing obsolete, recently fled Mount Velus.
Purphoros regrets my creation and wants to reforge me into something better.
Purphoros intended me to carry on his work by making even greater creations of my own.
Someone in Mount Velus implanted a terrible secret within me in order to smuggle it out into the world.

charoption.name: Cult of the Dragon Infiltrator
entries: You have infiltrated the ranks of the Cult of the Dragon. Having spied on the organization for quite some time, you are familiar with its inner workings and customs. You have a second identity as an initiate of the cult, enough of a facade to blend in as a simple grunt or servant.

charoption.name: Deep Delver
entries: You have a knack for making your way in the deep places of the world. You can recall the twists and turns of passageways and tunnels such that you can always retrace your steps underground. You're also well acquainted with foraging and survival in the Underdark, and can determine when sources of food and water are safe to consume. You can always find sufficient food and water for yourself and up to five other people in the Underdark, as long as sustenance is available in the area.

charoption.name: Doppelganger
entries: I'm a shapechanger. I have none of the traits of the race I'm imitating, but I retain my class features, background, and alignment. I have {@sense darkvision} out to a range of 60 feet. I can use an action to do either of the following at will:

I can innately cast {@spell detect thoughts}, requiring no components. My spellcasting ability is Intelligence. The spell's Wisdom save DC is 8 + my proficiency bonus + my Intelligence modifier. I can polymorph into any humanoid I have seen or back into my true form. My statistics, other than my size, don't change. Any equipment I'm wearing or carrying isn't transformed. I revert to my true form when I die.

charoption.name: Dragon Scholar
entries: You have studied dragons and their lore for many years. You can automatically identify locations built or used by dragons and can identify dragon eggs and scales by sight. If you fail an Intelligence check to recall lore relating to dragons, you know someone or some book you can consult for the answer unless the DM rules that the lore is unknown.

charoption.name: Drizzt Fan
entries: I once met the famous drow ranger Drizzt Do'Urden! In fact, I have a tattered piece of his famous green cloak and would never think to part with it.

charoption.name: Echoing Soul
entries: Your soul isn't your own or, at least, it wasn't always yours. Whether you've lived past lives, your soul was swapped into a different body, or you have a link connecting you to another being, you experience echoes from another life. These echoes grant you knowledge, talents, or even languages you can't always explain, but they also intrude on your perceptions and beliefs unexpectedly.
Roll on or choose an option from the Soul Echoes table to determine the nature of this Dark Gift. Additionally, you gain the traits that follow.

entries.caption: Soul Echoes
rows: My soul is linked with that of a person elsewhere, perhaps another domain, world, or plane.
I have lived many times before, my soul reincarnating each time I die rather than passing on.
My consciousness was removed from my original body and implanted in this one.
I was physically and spiritually merged with another being.
I share my body with an intangible, otherworldly force.
Time fractures around me, and I sometimes collide with my own past or future.

entries.name: Channeled Prowess
entries: You gain proficiency in two skills of your choice.

entries.name: Inherent Tongue
entries: You can speak, read, and write one additional language of your choice.

entries.name: Intrusive Echoes
entries: Immediately after you make an attack roll, an ability check, or a saving throw and roll a 1 on the {@dice d20}, your soul's memories emerge and overtake your perceptions and experiences. You might see people around you as someone other than who they are, or you become disoriented by a double-experience of the world around you. Roll on the Intrusive Echoes table to determine the effect of these vivid memories and perceptions. Once one of the effects occurs, these intrusive echoes can't manifest again until you finish a short or long rest.

entries.caption: Intrusive Echoes
rows: You are {@condition charmed} by a creature you can see (of the DM's choice) for 1 minute or until the creature damages you.
You are {@condition frightened} by a creature you can see (of the DM's choice) for 1 minute, or until the creature damages you.
You perceive another time or place around you until the end of your next turn. During this time, you are {@condition blinded} to your actual surroundings.
You perceive a different time or place overlapping your surroundings. Your speed is halved until the end of your next turn.
Memories and sensations overwhelm you. You are {@condition incapacitated} until the start of your next turn.
Your memory is one of triumph. You can reroll the ability check, attack roll, or saving throw that you just made. You must use the new roll.

charoption.name: Elusive Paramour
entries: A wealthy pasha in Calimshan has placed a bounty on my head for seducing his favorite concubine. Bounty hunters are scouring the Sword Coast in search of me, but I hope they'll never think to look in Icewind Dale.

charoption.name: Escaped Prisoner
entries: I was brought here from another world by spacefaring mind flayers. The ship in which I was imprisoned crashed in the mountains south of Ten-Towns. After surviving the crash, I nearly froze to death crossing the tundra to reach Ten-Towns. If some friendly trappers hadn't found me, I would have perished. I fear some of my captors also survived the crash and might come looking for me.

charoption.name: Gathered Whispers
entries: You are haunted by spiritual beings, whether the souls of the departed or entities from another plane. Their voices endlessly whisper, taunt, or cajole, sometimes rising to unearthly howls. Only you can perceive the spirits, unless you allow them to speak through you. The spirits are intangible and invisible; anyone who can see {@condition invisible} creatures sees only fleeting glimpses of these spirits as they haunt you.
Roll on or choose an option from the Whispering Spirits table to determine what haunts you. Additionally, you gain the traits that follow.

entries.caption: Whispering Spirits
rows: A council of my dead ancestors watches over me.
Fiendish presences vie for my soul.
Unquiet souls are drawn to me and beg for peace.
The spirits of those I killed linger around me.
An alien intelligence intrudes upon my thoughts.
A sibling I don't have shares my body.

entries.name: Spirit Whispers
entries: You learn the {@spell message} cantrip if you don't already know it, and require no components to cast it. When you cast the spell, the messages are delivered by one of your whispering spirits rather than you or the target's voice. Your spellcasting ability for this spell is Intelligence, Wisdom, or Charisma (your choice when you gain this Dark Gift).

entries.name: Sudden Cacophony
entries: When you are hit by an attack roll, you can use your reaction to channel your haunting spirits, letting their voices howl through you. If the attacker isn't {@condition deafened}, add your proficiency bonus to your AC against that attack, potentially causing it to miss. Once this trait causes an attack to miss, you can't use the trait again until you finish a long rest.

entries.name: Voices from Beyond
entries: Immediately after you make an attack roll, an ability check, or a saving throw and roll a 1 on the {@dice d20}, the haunting voices grow too loud to ignore. Roll on the Voices from Beyond table to determine the effect of these voices. Once one of these effects occurs, none of these haunting voices manifest again until you finish a short or long rest.

entries.caption: Voices from Beyond
rows: You have disadvantage on the next attack roll, ability check, or saving throw you make.
You are {@condition deafened} by the voices for 1 minute.

You are {@condition frightened} of the creature closest to you, other than yourself, until the end of your next turn. If multiple creatures are closest, the DM chooses which creature you are {@condition frightened} of.

Within the next 10 minutes, you can ask your spirits about the results of a specific course of action that you plan to take within the next 30 minutes. You can receive an omen as if you had cast the {@spell augury} spell. The omen manifests as whisperings from your spirits perceptible only to you.

charoption.name: Heroic Destiny
entries: Great deeds lie in your future, and it will take extraordinary effort to kill you before you accomplish those deeds. Choose or roll a random destiny using the Heroic Destiny table. Additionally, you gain the following traits.

entries.name: Defy Death
entries: You have advantage on death saving throws.

entries.name: Hard to Kill
entries: When you are reduced to 0 hit points but not killed outright, you can drop to 1 hit point instead. Once you use this trait, you can't use it again until you finish a long rest.

entries.caption: Heroic Destiny
rows: I'm destined to be the most skilled practitioner of a craft or trade.
I'm destined to earn a place among the stars of Nyx.
I'm destined to become a god.
I'm destined to liberate my beloved from the clutches of the Underworld.
I was born while a kraken ravaged Meletis, and I'm destined to destroy that kraken.
I'm destined to uncover the secret of the gods' power.

charoption.name: Hollow One
entries: As a Hollow One, the void left behind by your departed soul is filled with the strange magic of Blightshore. Becoming a Hollow One is a supernatural gift that bestows upon you the following traits.

entries.name: Ageless
entries: You don't age, and effects that would cause you to age don't work on you.

entries.name: Cling to Life
entries: When you make a death saving throw and roll 16 or higher, you regain 1 hit point.

entries.name: Revenance
entries: You retain your creature type, yet you register as undead to spells and other effects that detect the presence of the undead creature type.

entries.name: Unsettling Presence
entries: As an action, you can unsettle a creature you can see within 15 feet of you. The target has disadvantage on the next saving throw it makes within the next minute. Constructs, undead, and creatures that can't be {@condition frightened} are immune to this feature. Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a long rest.

charoption.name: Iconoclast
entries: No one can deny the reality of the gods of Theros, whose presence and deeds are visible in the night sky and sometimes directly in the mortal realm. But some people refute the idea that the gods are worthy of reverence. Such iconoclasts are common among the leonin, but members of any culture can adopt this supernatural gift. The Iconoclast Characteristics table presents suggestions for why you've become an iconoclast.
Your denial of the gods gives you supernatural power to resist their influence in the world. You gain the following traits.

entries.name: Enlightened Protection
entries: You can cast {@spell protection from evil and good} with this trait, targeting only yourself and requiring no material components. Once you do so, you can't cast it in this way again until you finish a long rest. Wisdom is your spellcasting ability for this trait.

entries.name: Reject the Gods
entries: You can't gain or lose piety to any god. You instead gain the following traits at the character level listed in each one. Wisdom is your spellcasting ability for any spell that you cast through these traits.

entries.name: Iconoclast Hero
entries: {@i 5th-level Iconoclast trait}
You can cast {@spell dispel magic} with this trait. Once you do so, you can't cast it in this way again until you finish a long rest.

entries.name: Iconoclast Paragon
entries: {@i 11th-level Iconoclast trait}
You can cast {@spell dispel evil and good} with this trait, requiring no material components. Once you do so, you can't cast it in this way again until you finish a long rest.
In addition, when you cast {@spell dispel magic} using your Iconoclast Hero trait, you cast it as a 4th-level spell.

entries.name: Iconoclast Archetype
entries: {@i 17th-level Iconoclast trait}
You can cast {@spell antimagic field} with this trait, requiring no material components. Once you do so, you can't cast it in this way again until you finish a long rest.
In addition, when you cast {@spell dispel magic} using your Iconoclast Hero trait, you cast it as a 5th-level spell.

entries.caption: Iconoclast Characteristics
rows: I blame the gods for the death of those I cared about.
Multiple gods seek to use me to their ends, so I try to avoid all divine entanglements.
It's obvious the gods are fickle and unworthy of worship.
I know the world's future lies with mortals, not gods.
I'm convinced the gods want me dead.
I refuse to be a pawn in divine schemes.

charoption.name: Inheritor
entries: An ancestor or mentor's deeds earned them a place in legend. Now it's your turn. You are the clear inheritor of a famed legacy. You've inherited a token from your predecessor, something that marks you as their inheritor, such as a signet ring, signature piece of clothing, or notable weapon.

Additionally, any time you reveal your legacy, you swiftly learn the local opinion of your predecessor. If locals have never heard of your predecessor, nothing changes. If they have, rumors of your connection spread swiftly, and many locals consider you either a hero or a threat. Heroes are welcomed and might easily gain an audience with local leaders. Threats are encouraged to leave before they invite danger.

charoption.name: Inscrutable
entries: Like a sphinx, you have a mind like a maze, impenetrable to mortal scrutiny. This might be a gift or training from an actual sphinx, the blessing (or curse) of a god, or an inexplicable talent. The Inscrutable Characteristics table suggests options for what makes you inscrutable. Additionally, you gain the following trait.

entries.name: Psychic Shield
entries: You have resistance to psychic damage.

entries.name: Sphinx's Shroud
entries: You are immune to any effect that allows other creatures to sense your emotions or read your thoughts. Wisdom ({@skill Insight}) checks made to ascertain your intentions or sincerity have disadvantage.

entries.caption: Inscrutable Characteristics
rows: I was educated by a sphinx in the Dakra Isles.
I am a devout adherent to one of Meletis's schools of philosophy (detailed in {@book chapter 3|MOT|3|Meletis}).
I only speak in the past tense, as if all things I say have already transpired.
I have sworn a vow to allow no living person to see behind the mask that covers my face at all times.
Why wouldn't I phrase every statement as a question?
I was born a sphinx, but a god cursed me into humanoid form and saddled me with the limits of mortal knowledge. I won't rest until I break the curse.

charoption.name: Lifelong Companion
entries: Behind many heroes is another hero whose greatness comes from the support and love they offer. Haktos had his beloved Perynes, Renata was accompanied by her servant Karados, and Siona sailed with her devoted crew. Like these partners, you are great and make others great. Consider the Companion Relationships table when determining your legendary connection. Any relationship with another player's character requires that player's consent. Additionally, you gain the following traits.

entries.name: Boon Aura
entries: Your allies within 5 feet of you have advantage on saving throws against being {@condition frightened} or {@condition charmed}, provided you aren't {@condition incapacitated}.

entries.name: Companion's Protection
entries: When a creature you can see within 5 feet of you is hit by an attack roll, you can use your reaction to cause the attack to hit you instead. Once you use this trait, you can't do so again until you finish a long rest.

entries.caption: Companion Relationships
rows: Another character is my lover or dearest friend.
Another character is my parent or child.
Another character is a champion of my god.
After admiring another character from afar, I've finally won a position by their side.
I want nothing more than for another character to recognize my devotion and love me in return.

charoption.name: Littlest Yeti
entries: I was raised by yeti. Although I relied on my ferocious guardians for food and warmth and never quite adapted to the cold, I speak Yeti and have advantage on Charisma checks made to influence yeti or improve their attitudes.

charoption.name: Living Shadow
entries: The shadow you cast is animate and ever-present, even when lighting conditions would otherwise prevent it. Your shadow occasionally moves out of sync with you. Sometimes it appears to be undertaking random but mundane tasks, while at other times it acts out your darker impulses, threatening or even attacking other shadows. With effort, you can bend this shadow puppetry to your will.
Roll on or choose an option from the Shadow Quirk table to determine how your living shadow behaves. Additionally, you gain the traits that follow.

entries.caption: Shadow Quirk
rows: My shadow often holds weapons or bears wounds that don't exist.
When I'm distracted, my shadow panics and tries to get other people's attention, as if it's desperate to escape me.
When it's not being watched, my shadow makes threatening gestures or creeps toward people.
My shadow's movements mirror mine incorrectly—when I raise my left hand, my shadow moves its right.
My shadow fiddles with or occasionally breaks Tiny, nonmagical objects.
There's a slight but noticeable delay between my movements and those of my shadow.

entries.name: Grasping Shadow
entries: You learn the {@spell mage hand} cantrip if you don't already know it, and require no components to cast it. The hand created by the spell is shadowy but is not bound to your actual shadow. Your spellcasting ability for this spell is Intelligence, Wisdom, or Charisma (your choice when you gain this Dark Gift).

entries.name: Shadow Strike
entries: When you make a melee attack roll, you can increase your reach for that attack by 10 feet. Your shadow stretches and delivers the attack as if it were you. You can use this feature a number of times equal to your proficiency bonus, and you regain all expended uses when you finish a long rest.

entries.name: Ominous Will
entries: Immediately after you make an attack roll, an ability check, or a saving throw and roll a 1 on the {@dice d20}, your shadow exerts a will of its own and might assist or hinder you or those around you. The next time you or a creature within 30 feet of you that you can see makes an attack roll, an ability check, or a saving throw, roll a {@dice d4}. If the number is odd, reduce the total by the number rolled. If the number is even, increase the total by the number rolled. Once this effect occurs, it can't happen again until you finish a short or long rest.

charoption.name: Midwinter Child
entries: Auril the Frostmaiden has blessed me, for I was born on the Midwinter holiday. I have resistance to cold damage.

charoption.name: Mist Walker
entries: The Mists grip all who tread the Domains of Dread, but you know how to slip through their grasp. You can navigate the Mists successfully given enough time and a little luck, but this freedom comes with a price; if you remain in one area for too long, the Mists find you and drain your life force.
Roll on or choose an option from the Misty Travels table to determine how you developed this Dark Gift. Additionally, you gain the traits that follow.

entries.caption: Misty Travels
rows: You learned a secret about the nature of the Mists. Ever since, you can manipulate them, but the lands you walk have turned against you.
You fled into the Mists to escape someone or something that's hunting you. You can never rest for long, knowing you're still being pursued.
You're part of an organization, a family, or an itinerant community with experience traveling the Mists. They taught you how to do the same.
The Mists stole you from your home and fractured your memories of where you're from. You've been on a quest to find your way back ever since.

entries.name: Misty Step
entries: You can cast the {@spell misty step} spell, requiring no spell slot, and you must finish a long rest before you can cast it this way again. Your spellcasting ability for this spell is Intelligence, Wisdom, or Charisma (your choice when you gain this Dark Gift). If you have spell slots of 2nd level or higher, you can cast this spell with them.

entries.name: Mist Traveler
entries: When you enter the Mists intent on reaching a specific domain, you are treated as if you possess a Mist talisman keyed to that domain. To use this trait, you must know the name of the domain you have chosen as your destination, but you don't need to have previously visited that land. This trait doesn't allow you to bypass domain borders closed by a Darklord's will.

entries.name: Poisoned Roots
entries: When you finish a long rest, the world around you in a 10-mile radius becomes a siphon that will eventually leech away your vitality. You can remain in the area safely for a number of weeks equal to your Constitution modifier (minimum of 1 week). Thereafter, each time you finish a long rest in the area, you must succeed on a {@dc 15} Constitution saving throw or gain 1 level of {@condition exhaustion} that can't be removed while you remain in the area.

charoption.name: Mist Wanderer
entries: The Mists whisper to you and guide you through their mysterious eddies. You immediately know if an object you're touching is a Mist talisman (detailed in {@book chapter 3|VRGR|3|Mist Talismans}). You recognize where the talisman originates from if you have been to its domain of origin.

charoption.name: Nyxborn
entries: Born from the minds of the gods, the creatures that populate the gods' realm are called Nyxborn. Nyxborn creatures resemble mortal beings, but philosophers debate their true character. Are they idealized forms of mortal beings, free from the imperfections and transience that cause mortals to suffer and die? Or are they hollow and soulless shades, lacking the authenticity and pathos that make mortal existence worthwhile?

A Nyxborn is like a fragment of divinity, an idea or a dream that is incarnate. You embody an idea—like the way leaves turn toward the sun or the feeling of ocean sand between the toes, the way the heart stirs when the tide of battle changes or the sadness that lingers when remembering a happy moment of childhood.

These ideas, dreams, memories, and feelings are the stuff Nyx is made of, and a Nyxborn is shaped from that raw material. You might have been specifically crafted by one of the gods to serve a certain purpose. Or your existence could be an accident caused by a confluence of supernatural forces. The Nyxborn Origin table offers a handful of suggestions that might explain how you came to be, and the Nyxborn Quirks table describes some special effects that might linger around your person.
Additionally, you gain the following traits.

entries.name: Cloak of Stars
entries: As an action, you wrap yourself in a starry cloak, appearing like a silhouette formed of the night sky. When you do, attack rolls have disadvantage against you. This cloak lasts for 1 minute, until you doff it (no action required), or until you die. Once you use this trait, you can't use it again until you finish a long rest.

entries.name: Nyxborn Resistance
entries: You have resistance to necrotic and radiant damage.

entries.caption: Nyxborn Origin
rows: One of my parents is a Nyxborn, a nymph, or some other supernatural creature.
I was formed from Nyx by one of the gods to serve as a divine emissary.
I'm a side effect of some other divine action.
A god witnessed my birth, making me what I am.
I was rescued from the Underworld and took on supernatural characteristics when I returned to life.
I'm a song or other work of art brought to life.
